pieces.doc: Visual fill paired with `[forMeter]`. Reflects `data-quality`, `data-percentage`, and the CSS custom property `--for-meter-percentage` so the consumer can drive width / transform from CSS.
Headless implementation of the [WAI-ARIA Meter pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/meter/), mirroring the HTML5 `<meter>` element semantics.

inputs.name: low
inputs.doc: Optional lower boundary of the "OK" range. Values below `low` are treated as below the comfortable region. `null` means no lower band.

inputs.name: high
inputs.doc: Optional upper boundary of the "OK" range. Values above `high` are treated as above the comfortable region. `null` means no upper band.

inputs.name: optimum
inputs.doc: Optional point at which the value is considered ideal. Falls back to the midpoint of `[min, max]`. Determines which region is `optimum`, which is `sub-optimum`, and which is `even-less-good` (see HTML5 spec).

inputs.name: getValueLabel
inputs.type: ((value: number, min: number, max: number) => string) | null
inputs.doc: Optional override for `aria-valuetext`. Receives the clamped value, `min`, and `max`.

models.name: value
models.doc: Two-way bindable. Current measurement, clamped to `[min, max]` for everything reflected on the host. The model retains what the consumer wrote so external bindings are not surprised.
